entries_new.name: Zona Franca La Plata
entries_new.story: Zona Franca La Plata is a free zone in Argentina. A committee document of the national Chamber of Deputies lists it among nine free zones in operation, with activity starting in February 1997, and gives no operator. Argentina's Free Zones Law 24.331 of 1994 lets the national government create one free zone in each province, plus up to four more nationwide, defining a free zone by reference to article 590 of the Customs Code.

entries_new.name: Zona Franca GIT El Alto
entries_new.story: Zona Franca GIT El Alto is a free zone in Bolivia that a 2019 University of Barcelona master's thesis lists as an industrial and commercial zone, one of seven it names among the country's free zones. The thesis gives no operator or opening year for it. The thesis describes Bolivia's free zones as created after Supreme Decree 22526 of 1990 came fully into force in 1991; in general a free zone is an area marked out by the authorities where tariff duties are not charged.

sources.t: Senia Andia Juárez, Incidencia de las exportaciones procedentes de zonas francas en el comercio exterior de Bolivia (Universitat de Barcelona master's thesis, December 2019)

entries_new.name: ZPE do Acre
entries_new.story: ZPE do Acre is an export processing zone (Zona de Processamento de Exportação, ZPE) in Acre, Brazil, listed as authorised in a 2020 guide by the tax publisher Econet. The guide gives no year or further detail. A May 2024 report in Movimento Econômico said only two of Brazil's 12 authorised ZPEs, those of Ceará (Pecém) and Parnaíba, were operating. Brazil's export processing zones are heavily incentivised areas for companies whose goods go only to export: federal import taxes and taxes on domestic purchases of equipment and inputs are suspended under Decree-Law 2.452 of 1988.

sources.t: Econet Editora: ZPE, Zona de Processamento de Exportação (2020)
Movimento Econômico: 10 ZPEs travam no Brasil, mas no Ceará e Piauí vão de vento em popa (2 May 2024)

entries_new.name: Free Economic Zone of Manaus
entries_new.story: The Free Economic Zone of Manaus (Zona Franca de Manaus, ZFM) is a free economic zone around Manaus, capital of Amazonas state in northern Brazil. Law 3.173 of 6 June 1957 formalised it, and Decree-Law 288 of 28 February 1967 redefined it with an area of 10,000 square kilometres and industrial and agricultural centres, to lift the Amazon out of economic isolation. The federal agency SUFRAMA, created in August 1967, administers its tax exemptions, which drew new investment by giving the region tax advantages over the rest of Brazil.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Free Economic Zone of Manaus

entries_new.name: Mariel Special Development Zone
entries_new.story: The Mariel Special Development Zone is a special economic zone at Mariel, Artemisa Province, about 40 kilometres west of Havana, Cuba, created in 2014 to attract foreign investment with tax and customs breaks; a former submarine base on the bay's west side was designated a free trade zone. Wikipedia says the zone is exempt from normal Cuban economic legislation: foreign investors pay 0.5 percent of income into a development fund and a 1 percent sales tax on local transactions. By late 2018, 17 foreign companies were operating there.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Mariel, Cuba

entries_new.name: Corozal Commercial Free Zone
entries_new.story: The Corozal Commercial Free Zone lies on the border of Belize and Mexico in Corozal District, northern Belize. Wikipedia says almost 65 percent of the district's people depend on it for jobs. Wikipedia gives no founding date, operator or details of its tax rules.

entries_new.name: Cayman Enterprise City
entries_new.story: Cayman Enterprise City is a special economic zone in the Cayman Islands launched on 3 February 2012 for knowledge-based industries, according to Wikipedia's list of special economic zones. Its incentives include no corporate, income or capital gains tax for businesses. The list gives no site; the entry has no pin.

sources.t: Wikipedia: List of special economic zones

entries_new.cov_type: Special economic zones and charter cities

entries_new.name: Zona Franca de Iquique (ZOFRI)
entries_new.story: The Zona Franca de Iquique (ZOFRI) is a free-trade zone in the port city of Iquique, Tarapacá Region, northern Chile, created on 25 June 1975 under the military government of Augusto Pinochet. Companies inside its 240-hectare walled enclosure trade goods free of duties and taxes. ZOFRI S.A., majority-owned by the state agency CORFO, runs it under a 40-year concession from the state and by law passes 15 percent of its revenue to municipalities in two regions.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Free Zone of Iquique

entries_new.name: Punta Arenas free port and free zone
entries_new.story: Punta Arenas, capital of Chile's southernmost region of Magallanes, has been one of Chile's two free ports since 1977, the other being Iquique, according to Wikipedia. Wikipedia's list of free economic zones also lists it among Chile's free zones. The sources give no operator or further detail; at Iquique, Chile's other free port, companies trade goods free of duties and taxes.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Punta Arenas

entries_new.laws: Common law of the State of Delaware as private law
entries_new.challenge: Honduran Congress repeal of the ZEDE regime (April 2022); Supreme Court ruling that ZEDEs are unconstitutional (September 2024)
entries_new.story: ZEDE Orquídea is a Zone for Employment and Economic Development (ZEDE) for agriculture at Las Tapias, in the municipality of San Marcos de Colón, Choluteca, southern Honduras, with Agroalpha as parent company. Wikipedia says Agroalpha planned a large greenhouse to grow produce for export and that the zone adopted the common law of the US state of Delaware as its private law. ZEDEs, created by a 2013 law, were zones with their own administrative, economic and judicial systems while still subject to the Honduran government. Congress repealed the regime in April 2022, and the Supreme Court declared it unconstitutional in September 2024. Wikipedia reports that the three existing ZEDEs claim 50-year protection under legal stability agreements, the ZEDE Organic Law and a bilateral investment treaty with Kuwait.
entries_new.anchor: San Marcos de Colón, Choluteca, Honduras

sources.t: Wikipedia: Zone for Employment and Economic Development

entries_new.name: Kingston Free Zone
entries_new.story: The Kingston Free Zone is one of Jamaica's free zones, in Kingston, established in 1976 next to the Kingston Container Terminal as Jamaica's first free zone, on a 180,000 square metre government-owned site. Businesses in Jamaica's free zones, set up under the Jamaica Export Free Zones Act, paid no tax on profits and no customs duties on imports and exports, and had to export 85 percent of their products outside CARICOM. entries_new.name: Puerto Chiapas Special Economic Zone
entries_new.story: The Puerto Chiapas Special Economic Zone (Zona Económica Especial) was one of seven special economic zones declared in Mexico under a law that President Enrique Peña Nieto signed in May 2016 to attract investment to southern states. The law firm Basham reported that the federal government published its declaration, among the first three, on 29 September 2017. The declaration was abrogated by a decree published on 19 November 2019, in force the next day, which ended the benefits granted to Mexico's seven special economic zones. Such zones offered income tax cuts for 15 years, a 0 percent VAT rate, a separate customs regime for foreign goods, and social security credits, in regions with the greatest development lags.

entries_new.name: Colón Free Trade Zone
entries_new.founder: Zona Libre de Colón (autonomous state entity)
entries_new.story: The Colón Free Trade Zone is a free port on Panama's Caribbean coast, near the Atlantic entrance to the Panama Canal, inside the city of Colón but outside its municipal jurisdiction. Decree Law 18 of 17 June 1948 created it as an autonomous state entity, and Wikipedia calls it the largest free port in the Americas, covering about 2.4 square kilometres. Companies there re-export goods to Latin America and the Caribbean; profits from foreign operations are exempt from income tax, while a 5 percent dividend tax and a yearly 1 percent tax on net worth apply. Decree Law 8 of 4 April 2016 updated its rules.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Colón Free Trade Zone

entries_new.name: Panamá Pacífico Special Economic Area
entries_new.founder: Agencia del Área Económica Especial Panamá Pacífico (APP)
entries_new.story: Panamá Pacífico is a special economic area and mixed-use development on the former Howard Air Force Base in Veracruz, Arraiján District, west of Panama City. Law 41 of 20 July 2004 created the Panamá Pacífico Special Economic Area and an independent agency (APP) to administer, regulate and promote it. A consortium of London & Regional Properties and Colombian banker Jaime Gilinski holds a 40-year licence from 2007 over 1,400 hectares, with a duty to invest US$405 million in the first eight years. Companies there get special tax, labour and legal incentives; Wikipedia counts more than 345.

sources.t: Wikipedia: Panama Pacifico

entries_new.story: Zona Franca Nueva Palmira is a free zone in Uruguay, listed in the investment agency Uruguay XXI's free zone brochure, located in the port town of Nueva Palmira in Colonia department. The brochure describes it as a state-owned zone for trade and logistics, including grain storage, and names it as one of the first two free zones, set up in 1923 under Law 7.593. Uruguay's free zones need prior state authorisation; any commercial, industrial or service activity is allowed, companies get a broad exemption from national taxes, and goods brought in are exempt from duties, while social security contributions for Uruguayan staff still apply.
